title: Effects of a ChatGPT-based flipped learning guiding approach on learners’ courseware project performances and perceptions
extended_summary:
This paper investigates whether integrating ChatGPT into a flipped learning environment can improve learners’ courseware project performance and related perceptions. The author argues that while flipped learning and project-based learning can provide more time for active work, teachers often struggle to give all students immediate, personalised guidance. The study therefore asks whether a ChatGPT-based flipped learning guiding approach (ChatGPT-FLGA) can outperform a traditional flipped learning guiding approach (T-FLGA) on project performance, self-efficacy, learning attitudes, motivation, and creative thinking.

The intervention was a ChatGPT-supported flipped learning system built by integrating ChatGPT with Tencent QQ. Students in the experimental condition received flipped classroom instruction plus AI-supported scaffolding through an “AI teacher” that provided instant personalised guidance, continuous conversation, smart reminders about assignments, and participation summaries. Both groups completed flipped learning activities and QQ-based discussions, but only the experimental group had access to ChatGPT-FLGA. Outcome measures included an objective project-performance rubric scored by two instructors and several self-report questionnaires, supplemented by post-study interviews.

Participants were 81 undergraduate students from two intact classes at a public normal university in Mainland China; they were taking a compulsory Modern Educational Technology course and had no prior knowledge of courseware design. One class of 42 students was assigned to the experimental condition and the other class of 39 students to the control condition, with the same teacher teaching both classes. The overall study lasted 8 weeks, including 3 weeks of initial instruction, pretesting in week 4, a 3-week intervention period, and posttesting in week 8.

The study concludes that ChatGPT-FLGA significantly improved project performance and several learner perceptions compared with traditional flipped learning. ANCOVA results showed significant advantages for the experimental group in project performance (F=8.32, partial η²=0.09), self-efficacy (F=4.45, partial η²=0.05), learning attitudes (F=5.10, partial η²=0.06), overall learning motivation (F=5.32, partial η²=0.06), intrinsic motivation (F=7.38, partial η²=0.09), and creative thinking tendency (F=6.85, partial η²=0.08), but not extrinsic motivation. Interview data suggested students valued the immediacy of feedback and personalised support. The author frames the findings as evidence that ChatGPT can serve as an effective scaffold in flipped higher-education project work, though generalisability is limited.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed quasi-experimental comparison with a control group, pre/post measurement, and statistical adjustment via ANCOVA, which supports moderate causal inference. However, it is not K-12, uses intact classes at a single university, and lacks random assignment at the individual level and some design details needed for the highest tier.
impact_tier_rationale: The study reports small-to-medium positive effects (partial η² from 0.05 to 0.09) on academic performance, attitudes, motivation, and creative thinking, indicating modest-to-moderate impact. Because the sample is a general higher-education population rather than the priority K-12 literacy population, impact is better classified as green rather than blue.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT-based flipped learning guiding approach in a higher-education multimedia courseware project, where students interacted with an AI teacher via Tencent QQ for instant personalized guidance, conversational scaffolding, reminders, and support during project-based flipped learning.
Traditional flipped learning guiding approach comparator using flipped classroom instruction, video/material access, and Tencent QQ-based discussion without ChatGPT-enabled AI tutoring.

finding.finding_summary: In a quasi-experiment with 81 pre-service teachers in China (experimental n=42, control n=39), the ChatGPT-based flipped learning guiding approach produced significantly higher multimedia courseware project performance than the traditional flipped approach after controlling for pretest scores. Posttest adjusted means were 89.93 vs. 87.13, with ANCOVA F=8.32 and partial η²=0.09, indicating a medium effect on vocational/educational technology project performance.
finding.measure: Rubric-scored multimedia courseware project performance across instruction, science, technology, artistry, and operability dimensions

finding.finding_summary: The ChatGPT condition significantly improved multiple learner perception outcomes relative to traditional flipped learning, including self-efficacy, learning attitudes, and overall learning motivation. Self-efficacy showed adjusted means of 34.77 vs. 33.14 (F=4.45, partial η²=0.05), learning attitudes 31.59 vs. 29.91 (F=5.10, partial η²=0.06), and learning motivation 26.01 vs. 25.14 (F=5.32, partial η²=0.06), all favoring the experimental group.
finding.measure: Self-efficacy scale, learning attitudes scale, and learning motivation questionnaire (Likert self-report)
finding.std_deviation: Self-efficacy SDs: 3.73, 4.54; Learning attitudes SDs: 2.76, 4.21; Learning motivation SDs: 2.37, 2.09

finding.finding_summary: Motivation effects were mixed when disaggregated: intrinsic motivation was significantly higher in the ChatGPT group, but extrinsic motivation did not differ significantly from the control group. Intrinsic motivation showed adjusted means of 12.74 vs. 12.12 (F=7.38, partial η²=0.09), whereas extrinsic motivation showed no significant difference (F=1.01, partial η²=0.01).
finding.effect_size: Intrinsic: partial η²=0.09; Extrinsic: partial η²=0.01

finding.finding_summary: Students using the ChatGPT-based flipped learning approach reported significantly higher creative thinking tendency than peers in the traditional flipped condition. Adjusted means were 19.07 for the experimental group and 17.40 for the control group, with ANCOVA F=6.85 and partial η²=0.08, suggesting a medium positive effect on a durable skill related to creativity.
finding.measure: Creative Thinking Tendency Scale (5-item Likert self-report)
